reference.view_jobs: A relationship needs a structured view when the reader must follow how parts relate, not only what each is. The kinds, each with the view that carries it: hierarchy or belonging (a tree); a call path from an entry to its effect (a call path); ordered steps with evidence (a trace); ordered work with branches (a flowchart or flow); participants exchanging messages over time (a sequence diagram); states and transitions (a state diagram); boundaries, ownership and dependencies (a board with arrows); records, identity and cardinality (an entity diagram); numeric change across ordered categories (a chart); the same questions answered for several items (a table); alternatives on corresponding topics (a comparison). A simple fact or an interpretation needs no separate view: prose under a purposeful heading carries it.

reference.detail: Long detail sits one action away (a tab, a disclosure, a linked page) so nothing becomes a text wall. Optional depth is what most readers skip under the current point: rationale, evidence, receipts, inventories or reference data. Content the point rests on stays in view: the exact corresponding facts the reader compares, and failure cases with their thresholds. A disclosure holds only the rationale or evidence about failure cases, never the cases themselves. Content carried from a source keeps its form and initial state; that can't be seen on the page.
